en.title: Korean 'The Intern' Remake Dethrones 'The Odyssey' at Box Office
en.summary: A fresh remake has captured the South Korean box office, ending a long reign. **The Intern**'s opening weekend success signals a shift in audience preference, proving remakes can still pack a punch.
en.body:
The South Korean box office has a new champion. The local comedy-drama remake **The Intern** has officially unseated the epic **The Odyssey** from its dominant position, drawing significant crowds in its opening weekend. **The Intern** welcomed 275,186 moviegoers over its first three days, demonstrating a strong appetite for familiar yet fresh storytelling.

While **The Odyssey** held onto the top spot for revenue, the admissions win for **The Intern** marks a significant shift. This new film is a South Korean adaptation of the 2015 American hit of the same name, which starred Anne Hathaway and Robert De Niro. Directed by **Kim Do-Young**, the remake stars veteran actor **Choi Min-sik** as a sixtysomething man who becomes an intern at a fashion company, forging an unlikely connection with the young CEO, played by **Han So-hee**. The adaptation thoughtfully shifts the narrative focus, leaning more into the CEO's personal and professional struggles rather than solely on the mentor-mentee dynamic, while also weaving in distinctly Korean cultural nuances and workplace dynamics.

## A New Generation Connects with a Beloved Story

The success of **The Intern** speaks volumes about the power of adaptation and cultural resonance. By infusing the original story with local flavor, director **Kim Do-Young** has managed to create a film that not only appeals to fans of the original but also captivates a new audience. The emphasis on generational friction and the complexities of modern Korean workplaces offers a relatable backdrop for viewers. This approach to storytelling has clearly resonated, allowing the film to break through the long-standing hold of a major international release.

## What the Box Office Numbers Mean

Audiences have shown a clear preference for **The Intern** in terms of sheer ticket sales, indicating a strong desire for local narratives that reflect their own experiences. The film's ability to draw over 275,000 viewers in its debut weekend is a testament to its broad appeal, challenging the notion that only tentpole blockbusters can dominate the box office. It suggests that well-crafted, character-driven stories, even those based on existing material, can achieve significant commercial success when they connect with the local cultural zeitgeist.

## What's Next

With **The Intern** now leading admissions, all eyes will be on its performance in the coming weeks to see if it can maintain its momentum. Fans can anticipate further analysis of its cultural impact and box office trajectory as it continues its run against other major releases.
